Madswimmers and the Dead Sea

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
They swum in the highest, coldest water in the world now they take on the lowest swim and its all for charity

Summary:
Madswimmer's world record highest swim in 2015 at 5909 m above sea level in the Andes in hypothermic conditions demanded a next chapter. Now they are taking on the Dead Sea, the lowest body of water on earth at minus 430 m below sea level.

So what’s so interesting about this swim you might say….

This is a far more dangerous swim, the effect of the water of the dead sea is so dramatic this becomes their most technical swim…the Madswimmer South African team will join Israeli, Jordanian and Palestinian swimmers to cross the Dead sea for the first time.

Dawn in the desert and the boats travel out to the Jordanian side of the Dead Sea, past border point and the always present guards with their guns.

It’s a 50 km swim that’s never been done before.

Swimming in the dead is a huge challenge, because of the salt content which is 10x more than that of the ocean, about 1/3 salt in fact, which not only makes the water so buoyant that it’s very challenging to swim or near impossible.

The atomic weight of the water is 2.5 times that of normal sea water, A 20 cm wave is like a baseball bat to the face, this means the weather is important and they have a three day window to swim.

One glass of dead sea water is enough to kill a person if there is no immediate help just one sip is enough to stop the swim, because of nausea, cramps and spasms… for safety there will be 3 medic’s on permanent watch.


Further information:
If you get the water in your eyes it’s like acid.. it will burn your eyes as if they have been set alight

Special masks have been designed for this swim and the swim will be done with mainly the arms, the legs need to balance the body,

Then there is the effects of salt on human skin especially if exposed for hours when swimming. Dehydration a very real problem.

To avoid the salt into the eyes and mouth, the swimmers had to train to swim with special masks which is a whole challenge by it self.  

The medics have insisted on pre swim checks as they are concerned about the length of time – 6 hours – in the water and the effects of the body.

The stroke will be freestyle without using a kick as the legs keep them balanced.
The Madswimmers do this for fun and charity, importantly they all pay their own way, any money raised goes to children’s charities. But this swim has another goal, the countries have joined forces to bring awareness to the fact that the Dead Sea is under threat and dying.

A programme for the New Year, January.

Press Release:


Madswimmers take on the Dead Sea
They’re not called mad swimmers for nothing. In 2015 they set a world record by swimming in the highest and coldest water in the world—in the Andes at 5909 metres above sea level, in hypothermic conditions. Now the team of swimmers have taken on their maddest and most dangerous swim for charity yet—17km across the Dead Sea where extreme salt content makes a gruelling swim, near impossible. Carte Blanche witnesses history in the making as so-called Madswimmers from Israel, New Zealand, Jordan, Palestine and South Africa brave the lowest lying body of water on earth.


Script:


V/O 13 and a half sec
The full moon’s still bright at 5 in the morning as a squad of small boats and rubber ducks speed eastwards from the Dead Sea’s Israeli shoreline…..in just under an hour they reach their destination, Jordan.
V/O 12 and a half sec
Its from here 28 swimmers will go for a world record being the first to swim across the Dead Sea…17.5 kms. 10 of these swimmers are South African
Jean: This swim has been two years in the making …

V/O 9 sec
Jean Craven heads up Madswimmers a group of ordinary South African’s who do extreme swims to raise money for children’s charities.

Jean: At the end of the day if we don’t get the necessary attention we don’t get funds so fortunately or unfortunately we have to go to extremes to do that and its for 18 charities 16 SA charities.

V/O 7 and a half sec
Last year Madswimmers created a world record, swimming in the highest, coldest body of water, in the Andes.

Jean It’s almost 6 000 metres above sea level It was touch and go until the last minute…by a mile one of the hardest swims we’ve done

V/O 15 sec
Their next challenge to swim in the lowest body of water and that’s the Dead Sea, 430 metres below sea level
Madswimmer, Evan Feldman was given the task of making this swim happen.
Evan: I started to research what happens to a human body after 8 hours in the Dead Sea nothing came up nobody has ever been in the water that long and I was researching and researching and trying to discover what ever I could and I came across a an indescript web page which spoke about somebody wanting to do the Dead Sea swim

V/O 6 sec
So Evan got in touch with Oded Rahav…. The result pure synchronicity.
Oded: They found us somehow on the internet and they made contact with one of our guys.

Evan: And I said Hi I’m Evan Feldman looking to swim in the Dead we want to cross from Jordan to Israel silence that’s what we were planning to It was a match made in heaven .


V/O 9 and a half
So the MADSWIMMERS joined forces with the Cyprus Israeli Swimmers and Eco Peace their aim to raise awareness of the plight of the Dead Sea..

Oded Rahav: You see back over there when I was a child I used to see the sea by the road and now its here that’s 2 kms ..in 25 years sea went down almost 30 m imagine vanished it’s a disgrace, and I think we can do something its like a person its still alive we can do something
V/O 18 sec
The Dead Sea, rich in minerals but over exploitation, water mismanagement and the surrounding nations diverting about 90% of the waters that have historically fed the Dead Sea are the cause of its depletion. Massive sinkholes which have swallowed roads and homes are one of the consequences

Oded: Each and every year we’re missing 1. 1 m going down …we cant afford it this is our Everest.

V/O 11 sec
There is a reason the Dead Sea has never been swum across, for a start the salt content of the water is 10 times that of the sea making it highly toxic
Evan: If you swallow even half a glass you are def out of the swim its life threatening in fact a small full glass of the `Dead Sea water is same poison as the bite of a rattle snake
Oded : Its not easy at all this sea is really harsh … its acid this water 36 % salinity, its not nice not for your eyes, your nose your throat and its not easy to swim your lower body floats so you work only with your upper body.

V/O 16 sec
The day before the challenge, the swimmers gather, practicing how to use the specially designed Tri Board breathing mask. For the South Africans this is the first time they have swam in the water and its about learning how to balance with your legs and swim with your arms.

Herman: What you realise is you have to do it extremely slowly otherwise you will CO2 in mask and you start getting headaches its really quiet different from anything else I have ever done.

V/O 7 sec
Three trauma dr’s will follow the swimmers bringing with them a range of equipment for possible emergencies.
Dani :There are a few dangers, long and prolonged effort in a hostile environment, swallowing the water will change you mineral content in blood, very high magnesium and calcium dangerous and aspirating water into your lungs can cause breathing problems.

V/O 11 sec
Permission to enter the Jordanian water was given only 24 hours before the start of the swim and with some inspiring words from Mayor Dov Litvinoff its all happening

Mayor Thank you everyone….

Evan I felt very excited I felt a little bit nervous this is pioneering stuff.

Kiki: We each have something inside of our self that drives us and you want to achieve something and this kind of swim does that you reflect on what you have done and what you can still do to make a difference in this world.

V/O 8 and a half sec
28 swimmers from Israel, South Africa, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, Jordan and Palestine take to the water

V/O 6 sec
They are divided into small groups, a support boat will monitor each pod of swimmers…

V/O 4 and a half sec
Very soon the the South Africans and 1 Israeli head into the distance

Jean: You know we had a good Israeli tour guide but hard swimming very hard swimming. ..we were front of the pack and we just kept the pace going…
V/O 9 and a half sec
In this highly salty, toxic water, stopping is essential, to carefully wipe the salt off your mask, spray the salt off your face, to drink…

Neil Up sound I can do 1. 07 I can do that
Neil : My first open water long swim it got difficult at parts but luckily I was swimming with good guys and they helped me get through the tough times.

Jean The salt is a diff animal from swimming point of view quiet toxic water a lot of guys chafing all over it’s a really tough swim a can understand why no one has done it before

V/O 13 and a half sec
The Dead Sea swim was a challenge not a race and so 7 hours after the start of this world first the swimmers congregate about a kilometer from the end and as one head for the shore

Abigail: Swimming this last 800 m and seeing the flags in distance and number of different countries that are here today that really inspires me

Evan: coming to the shore I didn’t want to take my mask off because I was crying my eyes out.

Hylton: My muscles were wanting to give up I got water in my eyes a lot but I didn’t want to give up…

Herman: If you don’t know what’s going to happen it makes it exciting and that’s why we do it it makes it exciting

GITA A short distance from the shore I started crying in my mask .For me it was hard the longest swim I have ever done and it was tough but done with so much camaraderie.

KIK… MS just been amazing blessed to have been part of this group
